description: Approved 2026-11-15 (/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-resource-destructors.html, ticket B; D1: the capture-free rule is enforced only by the runtime check in fz_make_resource). Today the stub keeps its dtor closure on the process heap, so each collection pre-walks the chain (mso_unreached_closures), speculatively forwards unreached closures (dead_closures HashMap), runs a second cheney_scan, sweeps, gathers DeadResource into a Vec, then queue_dead_resources boxes payloads into pending_dtors; sends deep-copy the closure; Cheney traces the closure edge. Change: Resource.destructor becomes a u64 literal closure word (replacing the always-noop extern C fn slot); fz_make_resource asserts the dtor ref is_literal ('a resource destructor captures nothing'). Stub shrinks 48 -> 16 B {shared_ptr, mso_next} (magic word is never read). One sweep: forwarded -> relink; BinRef -> shared_bin_release; Resource -> release_deferred returns Some((destructor, payload)) pushed straight onto pending_dtors as (literal word, raw u64); drain_destructors boxes the payload right before the call. release_resources_at_exit is the same sweep with nothing live. Remove: mso_unreached_closures, dead_closures, the second cheney_scan, DeadResource, queue_dead_resources, closure_of, closure_value/closure_value_set, closure offsets, RESOURCE_STUB_MAGIC, the closure trace in heap/gc/trace.rs, the closure copy in deep_copy (and gifts), fz_resource_destructor_noop, the dtor param of resource_alloc/ResourceHandle::new, the dtor call in fz_resource_release. Tests: a dead unclaimed resource queues (destructor, payload) with no heap word; a claimed one queues nothing; a capturing destructor is refused on all three paths (new fixture, expected error); dtors_dispatched unchanged across fixtures. Pins: stub-bearing heap figures fall by 32 B per stub and are lowered; any rise stops and is reported. Docs: .agent/docs runtime GC/resource sections, guides/memory.html, lib/kernel.fz make_resource doc (destructor captures nothing).
title: A resource's destructor is a code reference held by the shared Resource
